title: The return of the cassette tape
paragraphs: How do you consume your music? What format do you listen to it on? Technology now allows us to stream and download our favourite songs through websites and apps. This means it’s easy to access and it’s very portable, so we could enjoy it whenever and wherever we like. So, it’s surprising to know that the popularity of some old tech is increasing.

A number of musicians have been releasing their albums on vinyl and cassette tape. While this latter analogue technology lacks the good digital audio quality that we expect to hear today, in its heyday, it was a popular way for teenagers to enjoy recorded music. The introduction of the Walkman portable cassette player in 1979, made by Sony, meant people could listen to music on the move for the first time. By the end of 1989, 83 million tapes were bought by British music fans, but the invention of the compact disc in the 1990s changed that.

Despite the demise of the cassette tape in the 90s, in the first six months of 2020, nearly 65,000 music cassettes were sold in the UK, according to the Official Charts Company – double the sales from the same period the previous year. Although this is only a small fraction of overall music sales, cassette tapes are physical items that can be kept and collected – not stored in the cloud. And the resurgence of the cassette has been helped by big names such as Billie Eilish, Ariana Grande and Justin Bieber, who have released their music on this format.

To listen to music on a cassette, you need a tape player or a personal stereo to play them on, but this hasn’t deterred the new younger audience – its recent popularity seems to be more about buying memorabilia. Gennaro Castaldo from the British Phonographic Industry told the BBC: “Younger consumers are now buying into their collectible appeal – as they have done with vinyl – and the more they do this, the greater the demand for labels and artists to cater to.” But although cassettes won’t replace streaming as a way of listening to music, it does go to show how some tech never dies!

vocabulary.entry: consume /kənˈsjuːm/ v. 享用；消费
vocabulary.example: Nowadays, people consume most of their entertainment content online.
vocabulary.translation: 如今，人们的大部分娱乐内容都是通过网络享用的。

vocabulary.entry: format /ˈfɔːmæt/ n. 格式；载体形式
vocabulary.example: The video is available in MP4 format for download.
vocabulary.translation: 该视频提供MP4格式供下载。

vocabulary.entry: stream /striːm/ v. 流媒体播放（音乐、视频等）
vocabulary.example: She likes to stream classical music while she's working.
vocabulary.translation: 她喜欢在工作时流媒体播放古典音乐。

vocabulary.entry: portable /ˈpɔːtəbl/ adj. 便携的；手提式的
vocabulary.example: This portable speaker can be connected to your phone via Bluetooth.
vocabulary.translation: 这款便携音箱可以通过蓝牙连接到你的手机。

vocabulary.entry: vinyl /ˈvaɪnl/ n. 黑胶唱片
vocabulary.example: Many music enthusiasts still prefer listening to vinyl for its warm sound.
vocabulary.translation: 许多音乐爱好者仍偏爱黑胶唱片，因为它的音质更温润。

vocabulary.entry: cassette tape /kəˈset teɪp/ n. 盒式磁带
vocabulary.example: He found a box of old cassette tapes in his parents' attic.
vocabulary.translation: 他在父母的阁楼里找到了一盒旧的盒式磁带。

vocabulary.entry: analogue /ˈænəlɒɡ/ adj. 模拟的（与数字相对）
vocabulary.example: Analogue cameras have experienced a revival among photography lovers.
vocabulary.translation: 模拟相机在摄影爱好者中掀起了一股复兴热潮。

vocabulary.entry: heyday /ˈheɪdeɪ/ n. 鼎盛时期；黄金时代
vocabulary.example: The cinema was in its heyday in the 1950s and 1960s.
vocabulary.translation: 这家电影院在20世纪五六十年代迎来了它的鼎盛时期。

vocabulary.entry: recorded music /rɪˈkɔːdɪd ˈmjuːzɪk/ n. 录制音乐
vocabulary.example: Recorded music first became widely available in the early 20th century.
vocabulary.translation: 录制音乐在20世纪初开始广泛普及。

vocabulary.entry: on the move /ɒn ðə muːv/ 在路上；在移动中
vocabulary.example: The app allows you to access emails easily when you're on the move.
vocabulary.translation: 这款应用能让你在出行途中便捷地查看邮件。

vocabulary.entry: compact disc /kəmˈpækt dɪsk/ n. 激光唱片（CD）
vocabulary.example: Compact discs were once the most popular format for music distribution.
vocabulary.translation: 激光唱片曾是最主流的音乐发行载体。

vocabulary.entry: demise /dɪˈmaɪz/ n. 衰落；消亡
vocabulary.example: The demise of the local bookstore was caused by the rise of online shopping.
vocabulary.translation: 这家本地书店的消亡是由网购的兴起导致的。

vocabulary.entry: fraction /ˈfrækʃn/ n. 一小部分；微量
vocabulary.example: Only a small fraction of the population has access to this new technology.
vocabulary.translation: 只有一小部分人能接触到这项新技术。

vocabulary.entry: physical item /ˈfɪzɪkl ˈaɪtəm/ n. 实体物品
vocabulary.example: Collectors often value physical items more than digital versions.
vocabulary.translation: 收藏家通常更看重实体物品，而非数字版本。

vocabulary.entry: cloud /klaʊd/ n. 云（存储）
vocabulary.example: You can back up your photos to the cloud to avoid losing them.
vocabulary.translation: 你可以把照片备份到云端，以防丢失。

vocabulary.entry: resurgence /rɪˈsɜːdʒəns/ n. 复兴；再度流行
vocabulary.example: There has been a resurgence of interest in traditional crafts in recent years.
vocabulary.translation: 近年来，人们对传统手工艺的兴趣再度兴起。

vocabulary.entry: big name /bɪɡ neɪm/ n. 知名人士；大牌
vocabulary.example: The festival will feature performances by several big names in the music industry.
vocabulary.translation: 这场音乐节将有多位音乐界大牌登台表演。

vocabulary.entry: tape player /teɪp ˈpleɪə/ n. 磁带播放器
vocabulary.example: My grandfather still uses an old tape player to listen to his favourite operas.
vocabulary.translation: 我爷爷仍在用一台旧磁带播放器听他最爱的歌剧。

vocabulary.entry: personal stereo /ˈpɜːsənl ˈsteriəʊ/ n. 便携式立体声音响
vocabulary.example: The personal stereo was a must-have item for young people in the 1980s.
vocabulary.translation: 便携式立体声音响是20世纪80年代年轻人的必备单品。

vocabulary.entry: deter /dɪˈtɜː/ v. 阻止；打消……的念头
vocabulary.example: The high cost did not deter him from buying the rare book.
vocabulary.translation: 高昂的价格并没有打消他购买这本珍本书的念头。

vocabulary.entry: memorabilia /ˌmemərəˈbɪliə/ n. 收藏品；纪念品
vocabulary.example: The museum has a collection of sports memorabilia from the 20th century.
vocabulary.translation: 这家博物馆收藏了一批20世纪的体育纪念品。

vocabulary.entry: phonographic /ˌfəʊnəˈɡræfɪk/ adj. 与唱片相关的
vocabulary.example: The British Phonographic Industry represents the interests of record labels.
vocabulary.translation: 英国唱片业协会代表着唱片公司的利益。

vocabulary.entry: collectible appeal /kəˈlektəbl əˈpiːl/ n. 收藏价值
vocabulary.example: The vintage watch has great collectible appeal among watch enthusiasts.
vocabulary.translation: 这款复古手表在钟表爱好者中极具收藏价值。

vocabulary.entry: label /ˈleɪbl/ n. 唱片公司
vocabulary.example: The singer signed a contract with a major record label last year.
vocabulary.translation: 这位歌手去年与一家大型唱片公司签约。

vocabulary.entry: cater to /ˈkeɪtə tuː/ 迎合；满足……的需求
vocabulary.example: The restaurant caters to a wide range of tastes, from spicy to mild.
vocabulary.translation: 这家餐厅能迎合各种口味需求，从辛辣到清淡应有尽有。

sentences.english: How do you consume your music?
sentences.chinese: 你是通过什么方式欣赏音乐的？

sentences.english: What format do you listen to it on?
sentences.chinese: 你习惯用哪种格式听歌？

sentences.english: Technology now allows us to stream and download our favourite songs through websites and apps. This means it’s easy to access and it’s very portable, so we could enjoy it whenever and wherever we like.
sentences.chinese: 如今的科技让我们可以通过各类网站和应用程序流媒体播放或下载喜爱的歌曲，这意味着音乐不仅易于获取，还极具便携性，让我们随时随地都能享受音乐。

sentences.english: So, it’s surprising to know that the popularity of some old tech is increasing.
sentences.chinese: 但令人意外的是，一些老式音乐播放载体的受欢迎程度正在回升。

sentences.english: A number of musicians have been releasing their albums on vinyl and cassette tape.
sentences.chinese: 许多音乐人开始重新以黑胶唱片和盒式磁带的形式发行专辑。

sentences.english: While this latter analogue technology lacks the good digital audio quality that we expect to hear today, in its heyday, it was a popular way for teenagers to enjoy recorded music.
sentences.chinese: 尽管盒式磁带这种模拟技术，远不及如今我们熟悉的数字音频音质清晰，但在它的鼎盛时期，曾是青少年们欣赏录制音乐的主流方式。

sentences.english: The introduction of the Walkman portable cassette player in 1979, made by Sony, meant people could listen to music on the move for the first time.
sentences.chinese: 1979年，索尼公司推出了随身听便携式磁带播放器，意味着第一次人们可以随时随地聆听音乐。

sentences.english: By the end of 1989, 83 million tapes were bought by British music fans, but the invention of the compact disc in the 1990s changed that.
sentences.chinese: 到1989年底，英国乐迷共购买了8300万盒磁带，但20世纪90年代激光唱片（CD）的问世，彻底改变了这一局面。

sentences.english: Despite the demise of the cassette tape in the 90s, in the first six months of 2020, nearly 65,000 music cassettes were sold in the UK, according to the Official Charts Company – double the sales from the same period the previous year.
sentences.chinese: 据英国官方排行榜公司的数据显示，尽管盒式磁带在20世纪90年代逐渐衰落，但在2020年上半年，英国的音乐磁带销量达到了近6.5万盒，是前一年同期销量的两倍。

sentences.english: Although this is only a small fraction of overall music sales, cassette tapes are physical items that can be kept and collected – not stored in the cloud.
sentences.chinese: 虽然这一数字在音乐总销量中只占很小的比例，但磁带是实实在在的实体物品，可以被保存和收藏，而非存储在云端。

sentences.english: And the resurgence of the cassette has been helped by big names such as Billie Eilish, Ariana Grande and Justin Bieber, who have released their music on this format.
sentences.chinese: 此外，比莉·艾利什、爱莉安娜·格兰德、贾斯汀·比伯等知名艺人也纷纷推出磁带版专辑，进一步推动了磁带的复兴潮流。

sentences.english: To listen to music on a cassette, you need a tape player or a personal stereo to play them on, but this hasn’t deterred the new younger audience – its recent popularity seems to be more about buying memorabilia.
sentences.chinese: 想要播放磁带，你需要一台磁带播放器或便携式立体声音响，但这并没有打消年轻一代消费者的购买热情——磁带如今的流行，更多是因为它的收藏价值。

sentences.english: Gennaro Castaldo from the British Phonographic Industry told the BBC: “Younger consumers are now buying into their collectible appeal – as they have done with vinyl – and the more they do this, the greater the demand for labels and artists to cater to.”
sentences.chinese: 英国唱片业协会的詹纳罗·卡斯塔尔多在接受BBC采访时表示：“就像追捧黑胶唱片一样，年轻消费者如今正为磁带的收藏魅力买单。他们的购买热情越高，唱片公司和艺人就越愿意迎合这种需求。”

sentences.english: But although cassettes won’t replace streaming as a way of listening to music, it does go to show how some tech never dies!
sentences.chinese: 尽管磁带不会取代流媒体成为主流的音乐播放方式，但这也恰恰印证了一个道理：有些老物件永远不会彻底退出历史舞台。
